prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)CCNCc1ccc(-c2ccc3ncnc(Nc4ccc(OCc5cccc(F)c5)c(Cl)c4)c3c2)o1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL203

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of epidermal growth factor receptor kinase (unknown origin) using [33P]-ATP after 20 to 30 mins by radiometric assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of His-tagged EGFR cytoplasmic domain (645-1186 aa) (unknown origin) assessed as inhibition of autophosphorylation by TR-fluorometry
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call":"NOT_COMMENSURABLE","confidence":0.72,"error_class":"assay_method","reason":"Lapatinib is a slow-binding, conformation-sensitive EGFR inhibitor, so a short radiometric kinase assay and a cytoplasmic-domain autophosphorylation TR-fluorometry assay can yield IC50 values differing by over tenfold."}

parsed.reason: Lapatinib is a slow-binding, conformation-sensitive EGFR inhibitor, so a short radiometric kinase assay and a cytoplasmic-domain autophosphorylation TR-fluorometry assay can yield IC50 values differing by over tenfold.
